title: Pipe Manifold
model_title: Pipe Manifold (Distribution Header with Valved Branches)

introduction.definition: A pipe manifold (header) is a large pipe that distributes flow to — or collects flow from — several branch lines. Each branch has an isolation valve so it can be opened, closed or maintained independently. Headers keep velocities low so all branches receive similar pressure.
key_points: Header area ≥ sum of branch areas helps even distribution
Drains at low points, vents at high points
introduction.summary: A pipe manifold (header) collects or distributes flow among several branches from one large pipe. Each branch has its own isolation valve so lines can be opened, closed or maintained independently — typical of cooling-water, steam, gas and chemical distribution.

video_tutorials.title: Pipe Manifold — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Pipe Manifold.
A pipe manifold (header) is a large pipe that distributes flow to — or collects flow from — several branch lines.
Each branch has an isolation valve so it can be opened, closed or maintained independently.
Headers keep velocities low so all branches receive similar pressure.
Typical applications include cooling-water and steam distribution; pump suction and discharge headers; gas and chemical distribution; well-test and sampling manifolds.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction.
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

video_tutorials.title: Pipe Manifold — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Pipe Manifold.
Check branch valve positions and leaks.
Drain sediment.
Inspect header for corrosion at dead legs.
Watch for uneven distribution: far branches starved. Common cause: undersized header.
Watch for dead-leg corrosion: pitting. Common cause: stagnant ends.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
